First listed 2026-07-29 · episode or wrap

The Real Estate Brokerage War, For-Profit Education, & the Art of the Short with Brad Safalow

Safalow favors Zillow over Compass, expects housing affordability to improve with lower rates, and argues that AI weakens Google advertising and education economics. He revisits shorts in Trupanion, Freshpet and Kinsale. Eisman explicitly shares selected education and pet-insurance concerns while disclosing Google ownership. Primary records confirm Washington listing restrictions, computing-enrollment declines and Kinsale premium softness, but challenge zero-growth pet insurance and simple Freshpet deterioration. Several private channel checks, liability accusations and valuation claims remain unresolved. The interview was recorded June 11, well before publication.

Substack · 2026-07-29 ↗
The episode offers differentiated mechanisms but many causal claims depend on private research. Keep Safalow stock calls separate from Eisman ownership and explicit endorsements. Subsequent operating results are mixed rather than uniform confirmation of the short theses.

How he reasons here

  • Separate listing access from brokerage brand and lead generation.
  • Trace commission incidence and agent-broker splits.
  • Compare housing supply with household formation by region.
  • Distinguish price, revenue growth, dilution and cash generation.
  • Test insurance pricing with cohort aging and adverse selection.
  • Distinguish advertising claims from product safety.
  • Treat private research and management guidance as hypotheses requiring independent checks.
